summary: Edge proxy host-rewrite caused EU requests to egress to US region, P95 spike
description: Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-09 14:05 UTC FinSight reported a sudden increase in p95 generation latency for requests that are region-pinned to eu-west-1. Support observed that a subset of their requests were serviced from us-west-1 instead of eu-west-1, leading to ~200-300ms extra latency and token throughput degradation. Impact: customer-facing latency spikes and degraded SLO compliance for enterprise workload. Immediate customer impact: higher tail latency, some timeouts on interactive workflows. Hypothesis: an edge proxy configuration change rewrote Host/SNI or forwarded a rewritten header causing control-plane routing to select a US egress. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and follow-up hardening.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer uses region pinning header X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1.
2) Send 1000 short-chat requests over 3 minutes.
3) Observe successful responses but p95 shows sporadic spikes; traces show egress address us-west-1.
4) Re-run while capturing edge-proxy access logs and control-plane routing logs to correlate host header and selected egress node.
logs:
[2026-03-09T14:06:12Z] edge-proxy-02 request_id=abc123 host=eu.api.redwood.internal forwarded_host=eu.api.redwood.internal rewrite_host=us.api.redwood.internal selection=eastus-us-west-1
[2026-03-09T14:06:12Z] control-plane route_decision request_id=abc123 chosen_pool=us-west-pool score=0.73 pin_match=true
[2026-03-09T14:06:12Z] serving-runtime us-west-1 instance=svc-07 produce_token_latency=210ms
investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-09 14:20 UTC: reproduced with synthetic client; captured headers show X-Forwarded-Host and Host were rewritten in-flight on a subset of edge proxies.
- Checked recent deploys: edge-config PR #5241 merged 2026-03-09 13:58 UTC introduced an optional host rewrite to implement path-based routing for a canary partner.
- Correlated requests that landed in us-west-1 to a small pool of edge proxies (edge-proxy-02, edge-proxy-05). Those proxies had canary flag enabled.
- Control-plane routing policy prefers SNI/Host when deciding regional affinity; when Host is rewritten to us.api..., affinity favors US pool despite X-Redwood-Region pin header being present (bug in precedence logic).
- Temporary mitigation: rolled back PR #5241 on 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC and disabled canary on edge-proxy-02/05 which stopped the cross-region egress.
- Still investigating why X-Redwood-Region pin header was not given precedence over host-based affinity in routing decision.
comments: Elena Park (2026-03-09): Customer reports spikes in p95 and included example request IDs and traces. Initial triage assigned to infra on-call.

Marcus Chen (SRE) (2026-03-09): Noticed host rewrite on a subset of edge proxies. Escalated to edge team, flagged potential regression from last config roll. Adding control-plane oncall @sanjay to verify routing precedence.

Sanjay Reddy (Control Plane) (2026-03-09): Confirmed precedence bug: host-based affinity was evaluated before explicit region pin header when SNI present. Creating hotfix branch to invert precedence and add test coverage. Patch queued.
Marcus Chen (2026-03-10): Rolled back edge-config PR #5241 as emergency mitigation at 03:40 UTC. Customer confirmed improved p95 within 10 minutes. Monitoring for 24h.
FinSight Ops (customer) (2026-03-10): Confirmed tail latency returned to baseline after rollback. Requesting postmortem and timeline because this impacts compliance reporting.
Marcus Chen (2026-03-11): Postmortem drafted; hotfix PR #5250 created to ensure X-Redwood-Region header precedence and to add canary gating checks. Tests added to e2e routing suite.
resolution: Mitigation: Rollback of edge-config PR #5241 and canary disabling on affected edge proxies restored correct region affinity and reduced p95 to baseline. Fix: control-plane precedence logic updated (hotfix PR #5250) to respect explicit region pin headers over host-based affinity; added unit and e2e tests. Follow-ups: 1) formal postmortem and timeline to be shared with customer; 2) add synthetic canary that asserts region-pinned traffic does not egress cross-region; 3) improve observability: track header vs host mismatches in routing dashboard. Planned release of hotfix to prod after validation window 2026-03-13.
follow_up_actions:
- Action 1: Release hotfix PR #5250 and verify in canary pool by 2026-03-13.
- Action 2: Create synthetic test that asserts X-Redwood-Region will always win routing decision; add to daily synthetic suite.
- Action 3: Update runbook to include steps for quickly disabling host rewrite canaries.
- Action 4: Customer outreach: provide detailed timeline and evidence for compliance team (owner: CS lead).
